summary: Both editions were independently compared with every clause of the supplied working Greek across sections i–ii. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the road comparison, complete virtue and vice lists, speaker changes, wholehearted turning to the Lord, both necessity assertions, and the positive and negative work clauses. The simplified edition’s sentence restructuring does not materially change these claims. Reader-facing “servants” follows current policy, and “turns to the Lord” preserves the distinct source expression rather than imposing a uniform repentance formula. Bracketed material remains visibly distinguished, and the notes disclose reported alternatives and editorial corrections without replacing the selected working readings. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied source and consistency with the attributed comparison reports; it does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript handwriting, photographs, or an exhaustive collation.
